title: PentAGI deep-dive + reusable components report — identify directly portable code
goal: Investigation task (no code edits). Deep read of PentAGI (https://github.com/vxcontrol/pentagi, MIT licensed, 12.5k stars). Identify: (a) which specialist prompts can we directly port? (b) which planner logic patterns? (c) which test/eval infra? Deliverable is research report at docs/research/pentagi-component-reuse.md.
scope: (1) Clone + study PentAGI source. (2) Per component (Researcher, Developer, Executor, Planner, Memorist agents): assess port-ability. (3) Report at docs/research/pentagi-component-reuse.md with: component name + LoC estimate + license-compat check + recommended action (port-as-is | adapt | ignore). (4) Per-action: list our existing code that would be replaced/extended. NO code changes in this task.
generation_reason: Per Codex: 'niet forken voordat we precies weten wat herbruikbaar is'. We've referenced PentAGI in many design discussions; now formal eval. Per ANTI_DRIFT.md Rule 1: metric is 'identified reusable components count + recommendations'.

constraints.active_task_gate: Single active task AND ANTI_DRIFT.md loaded.
constraints.scope_creep_guard: Investigation + report only. NO code edits in production.
constraints.license_check: Verify MIT compatibility before recommending port. Document any caveats.
constraints.deliverable_is_report: Output is markdown research report, not code.
